key_insight: Colorectal cancer prediction improved with longer EHR lookback, reaching about 80% of the observed AUROC gain within 10 years and plateauing around 18 years.
clinical_relevance: Historical primary-care records may add predictive information, but the modest discrimination does not establish clinical utility.
method: Pretrained a 34.6M-parameter decoder-only transformer on 1.4B coded events from 3.6M patients.
Fine-tuned for incident colorectal cancer prediction with a 12-month pre-diagnostic buffer.
Compared 15 nested lookback windows spanning 2–30 years within the same cohort and against XGBoost.
evidence_signal: Among 1,008 cases and 9,582 matched controls registered for at least 30 years, transformer AUROC rose from 0.551 at 2 years to 0.590 at 18 years; XGBoost peaked at 0.589.
watch_item: Findings from patients with at least 30 years of registration in one UK region may not generalize to populations with shorter or fragmented records.
paper_title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
